title: Dongria audio holdings in the Frobenius Middle-India Archive
status: collection-level evidence verified; public retrieval exhausted for this pass; access enquiry prepared but unsent

source.title: Written Legacies — Middle-India Archive
source.locator: Written Legacies, Roland Hardenberg paragraph, second research collection
source.inspection: Institutional category page full extracted text; dedicated page text recovered through search after direct fetch cache miss. Both are the same institutional source, not independent corroboration.

findings: The institute describes ethnographic material from Roland Hardenberg’s 2001–03 research among Dongria Kond in Rayagada district.
Its description includes field diaries digitised by Hardenberg in 2005, with observations, sketches and interviews.
The same collection includes WAV recordings of songs at dance events and recitations attributed to ritual specialists described as Bejuni and Jani.
The institute describes researcher access on request. No request was sent.
distinctions: 2001–03 is the described research period, not an inspected date for an individual audio item.
2005 refers to the diaries’ digitisation, not necessarily audio digitisation or performance.
The earlier Puri 1995–96 materials in the same paragraph are a separate collection.
Niggemeyer Kuttia Kond material is not Dongria fieldwork.
No link to Dambu Praska, the Lament film or the CircaFilms soundtrack is established.

retrieval_attempts.result: Web-tool timeout; no catalogue records retrieved.
No item-level record recovered in returned search results.

editorial_decision: Retain as a concrete archival route in KB. Do not add claims about recordings to the article before item metadata or audio inspection. The finished manuscript remains current.
next_action: Reopen on a working catalogue/finding aid or an archive response. Do not repeat identical catalogue attempts. Sending the prepared enquiry requires explicit user authorization; continue other public research independently.

followup.finding: The German institutional description also specifies research access on request. It describes Hardenberg’s deposit as a Vorlass; this is not evidence that he is deceased. The English and German descriptions are one institutional evidence family.
catalogue_access: Chrome navigation timed out; catalogue content was not loaded.
German-language and finding-aid searches did not recover individual Dongria audio records.
followup.interpretation: Access failures do not establish that records are absent or restricted. No item count, shelfmark, performer identity, track language or exact performance date established.

unsent_request.intended_recipient: Frobenius Institute, Middle-India Archive team; address not yet verified
unsent_request.subject: Finding aid for Roland Hardenberg’s Dongria Kond audio recordings, 2001–03
unsent_request.body:
Dear Middle-India Archive team,

I am preparing a sourced editorial series for Project Odisha on Dongria Kondh life and cultural knowledge. Your Written Legacies page describes Roland Hardenberg’s 2001–03 Rayagada fieldwork materials, including recordings of songs at dance events and recitations by Bejuni and Jani ritual specialists.

Could you point me to a finding aid or catalogue entry for this collection? I would welcome item identifiers and any available metadata for recording dates, villages, performers, occasions and languages, together with links to associated field notes or transcriptions. Please distinguish metadata that is documented from later attribution.

Could you also explain eligibility and procedures for research listening access, any restrictions on culturally sensitive material, and the separate requirements for quoting translations or reproducing audio? At this stage I am seeking catalogue information and access guidance, not requesting publication permission for an identified recording.

Thank you,
Ahimanikya Satapathy
Project Odisha
